memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: I myself will call to account anyone who does not listen to my words that the prophet speaks in my name. - Deut 18:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God adds a solemn warning to His wonderful promise. To ignore the words of the promised Prophet is no small matter, "I myself will call to account anyone who does not listen." The privilege of hearing God's words through this Prophet came with real responsibility. To turn away from Him was to turn away from God Himself.

This is sobering but important. God takes His Word seriously, and how we respond to His Son matters eternally. Because Jesus is the Prophet who speaks God's very words, refusing to listen to Him is not a neutral choice, it is a rejection of God's own voice.

We must not hear this only as a threat, but as a loving warning. God tells us how serious it is precisely because He wants us to listen and live. The New Testament echoes this, warning us not to neglect so great a salvation and to pay careful attention to what we have heard (Heb 2:1-3). The wonderful news is that listening to Jesus leads not to condemnation but to life. Those who hear His voice and follow Him have eternal life and will never perish (John 10:27-28). God's call to account is real, but so is His open invitation to come, listen, and live. Are you truly listening to Christ, or letting His words slip past you?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you truly listening to Christ, or letting His words slip by?
2. What might it look like to take His words more seriously?
3. How does His invitation to life encourage you to listen?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me never neglect the words of Your Son. Give me ears that truly listen and a heart that gladly obeys. Amen.
